page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top centre, page number at the top right. Line numbers (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35) in the left margin. Text runs from the top, then a centred chapter heading "L. CHRONOLOGIA SACRA.", then paragraphs I to IV.

main_text.l: pocryphis iam olim reiectis nihil attinet dicere.
XI. Historia humana in solidum fidem me-
retur, si historiographus per omnes partes im-
plesse suum munus deprehendatur. Officium i-
stud in tribus est positum, diligentiâ, iudicio, & fide Dili-
gentia poni debet in colligendâ scribendorum materiæ, vt
proferantur illa, quæ digna sunt luce. Iudicio opus est, vt
videat historicus quibus credat. Fides denique in eo spe-
ctatur, vt in narratione historiæ nuda veritas exponatur,
siue illa, quæ gesta sunt, probentur scribenti, siue impro-
bentur. Sed accingamur ad scriptionem systematis histo-
riæ sacræ, idque in epitome historico-chronologica, i-
tem in prosopographiâ & topographiâ sacrâ. Priùs tamen
indicemus modum Chronologiæ sacræ.
L. CHRONOLOGIA SACRA.
I. CHronologia sacra est temporis notatio
historica ex S. literis petita. Proinde, vt
historia, sic etiam chronologia, ad varias artes & faculta-
tes pertinet. Cæterùm chronologia solet appellari alter
historiæ oculus.
II. Eius partes duæ sunt: prima de affectio-
ne temporis historici, altera de ipsius partitio-
ne. Cum partitione cohæret explicatio.
III. Tempus historicum in sacris habet af-
fectionem analogam & anomalam.
IV. Affectio analoga temporis sacri est par-
tim ordo & duplicatio, partim rotundatio &
variatio. Ordo temporis chronologici in Scriptura sacra est
triplex, naturæ, dignitatis, & prudentiæ: siue, vt alii lo-
quuntur, est ordo naturalis, personalis, & historicus. Ordo
natura, seu generationis, est, cum id, quod natura & exi-
stentiâ

page.notes: Left margin also shows stray marks and line numbers at the far left edge (such as "10", "0", "s") that belong to the neighbouring page or show-through; not transcribed. The first word of the page is a fragment ("pocryphis"), kept as printed. The word "Priùs" and "tamen" are read with some doubt ("ramen" in the scan). "Ordo natura" is read as printed; the italic "natura" may be a typesetting variant. The final line "stentiâ" is printed on the next line as "stentiâ" and is joined to "exi-" as "existentiâ". Line numbers 5 to 35 are printed in the margin and are given as notes.
